_note: Pushed to the master 2026-08-09 as aid 23262946: 11 questions, 100 points (8/9/9/10/9/9/9/9/10/9/9), every part filled and submitted in Teacher Preview and every one graded correct. Every source problem reads a FIGURE, and the two box plot questions the bank already had hand the five-number summary over as text -- so 'read a box plot' tested reading a sentence. The eight new ones draw it. All plotted values are multiples of ten so anything a student reads off lands on a labelled tick, and the section widths come from a fixed set in rotated order so no two quarters can tie. Three of the eight target a specific misconception: a wide box means more data, a long whisker means an outlier, and the median sits at the center of the box.

questions.title: Read a Box Plot - Take the median and the quartiles off a drawn box plot, compute the interquartile range, and identify which quarter of the data is the most spread out

Where the Median Sits Inside the Box - A box plot whose median line is well off center; read it, compare the two halves of the middle fifty percent, and say what an off-center median reveals about the shape of the data

Spread Within Each Quarter of a Box Plot - Find which quarter of a box plot has the smallest spread, read that spread and the interquartile range, and compare two intervals with the 25%-per-quarter rule

Outlier Check from a Box Plot - Take the quartiles off a drawn box plot, build the 1.5 times IQR fences from them, decide whether a newly measured value is an outlier, and separate a long whisker from an outlier

What a Box Plot Does Not Show - Compare two box plots with the same range but different box widths and sample sizes to see that a wider box means more spread, not more data, and that a box plot never shows counts at all
Compare Three Box Plots - Read three box plots on a shared axis to find the largest median, find one group's IQR, and say what comparing medians does and does not tell you
Box Plot from a Frequency Table - Read the minimum, first quartile, median and third quartile off a frequency table so the finished box plot can be checked against them
Box Plot and Histogram of the Same Data - Read a class count only the histogram shows, then judge which display reveals a second hump and which gives the IQR directly
Boxplot - IQR, Fences, and Outlier Check (Context) - From a five-number summary in context, compute IQR and the 1.5*IQR fences, then decide whether a new observation is an outlier

Five-Number Summary from an Unsorted Data Set - Sort a set of readings recorded out of order, find the two quartiles and the median, and compute the interquartile range that spans the middle half of the data

Build the Five-Number Summary from Raw Data - From an unsorted list of eleven measurements, enter the minimum, first quartile, median, third quartile and maximum, then give the interquartile range and say what the box of a box plot spans
Pre-FRQ Grade an Outlier Check - The scenario and grading checklist of the five-number-summary FRQ, but the student grades four sample responses against the rubric instead of writing one
